name: Documentation coverage and voice check
scoped_purpose: Use for: letting a newcomer or an AI learn the runner from its documents, by checking links, index reachability, coverage of variables, subcommands and public names, and house voice. Avoid: judging whether the prose is clear or correct, and checking examples by running them.
milestones: 1. Documentation coverage and voice conformance: no document fails the em dash cases when re-recorded.
knowledge: Documentation drifts unless coverage is generated from the repository: cases are produced from the code and a coverage case fails when a document or variable has no case. The house voice forbids em dashes, and a mechanical replacement changes meaning, so each is rewritten by hand.
measures_of_success: Every generated documentation case passes: no broken link, no document unreachable from the index, nothing undocumented, no em dash.
parameters: The documents folder, an index file, a generated configuration reference, and the generator that produces cases.
inputs: The markdown files, the package's public names and the real argument tree.
outputs: Pass or fail per case, naming the broken link, missing description or offending document.
effects: None; documents are read only.
usage_notes: Update the index when adding a document, document each new variable and subcommand, and regenerate cases rather than hand-editing them.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Scoped prediction store
scoped_purpose: Use for: keeping what an anticipation engine learned (recurring-ask patterns, live predictions with precomputed views, an outcome log) per scope across turns and restarts. Avoid: judging whether predictions are right, which is not measured here, and cross-scope sharing.
knowledge: The store sits behind a port so a consumer with its own database can supply one. Storage must be best-effort and never raise into a turn. Prediction quality is a separate unmeasured question: the engine logs each prediction against the actual next message, but no replayed corpus scores it.
measures_of_success: A store passes every contract scenario: round trip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart and tolerance.
parameters: A scope key per call, patterns, predictions with an expiry time and optional views, and a log record.
inputs: Pattern and prediction records and the scope key.
outputs: The saved patterns, the unexpired predictions, a precomputed view text by prediction id, or nothing for a write.
effects: Writes persistent state (a file per scope and an outcome log in the file store) and drops expired predictions on load.
usage_notes: Implement the port's methods to add a backend and run the same contract scenarios against it; choose the file store for a lane, an in-memory store only as a reference.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Autopilot run-or-skip gate
scoped_purpose: Use for: deciding per quest, before any goal is read or model called, whether a recurring autopilot pass should work now, according to the person's settings. Avoid: judging what a pass does once it runs, and whether the moment suits the person.
knowledge: A wrong run spends and sends against the person's setting, and a wrong skip loses a day, so the gate is a rule, not a quality dial. Cadence is judged in the quest's own time zone with a roster of days, not by elapsed time, and a pending Run now request or a reactive trigger can override cadence. Backpressure also holds a quest.
measures_of_success: Every labelled gate case ends as skipped for the right reason or as past every gate, and a baseline that uses elapsed-time cadence with no roster fails the cases.
parameters: A daily budget, a backpressure flag, a clock, and per-quest autopilot settings (cadence, Run now, reactive trigger, roster days).
inputs: The quest list, each quest's autopilot settings, open tasks and asks, open decisions, and the current time.
outputs: For each quest, either a skip with a reason or passage through every gate to the work stage.
effects: Counts against the daily budget when a quest is worked; before the gates pass, no goals are read and no model is called.
usage_notes: Place every eligibility rule in the gate, before any expensive read, and add a case for each new rule or setting.

name: Evolve by metric
scoped_purpose: Use for keeping every part of QAR specified as a solution with alternatives, a metric and a selected implementation, so the best one is used as the state of the art moves. It avoids saying what QAR is for: that is the top intent, and the general machinery for checking, measuring and selecting is the evolvable-structure library's.
knowledge: The author's evolvable structure (intents, problems, solutions, implementations, ideals and metrics); the evolvable-structure library's checks, measurement harness and selector.
measures_of_success: Every solution has a recorded result on committed code, selections follow the measurements, and Joshua can steer by reviewing metrics without reading code. Standing conditions: Every part of QAR has a record, a current measured result and a selection that follows the measurement; a better model, method or tool replaces the current one without a rewrite.
parameters: The records under esoi, the esoi configuration, the evaluation components.
inputs: A change to the code, a new alternative, or a new model or tool to compare.
outputs: Checked records, recorded metric results and the selected implementation for each solution.
effects: Result rows are appended to the evaluation log; no model spend unless a paid arm is run by decision.
usage_notes: Run esoi check before committing and esoi run --stale after committing measured code. Paid arms follow the metric run policy.

name: Intent frame for quest-scoped prompts
scoped_purpose: Use for: telling every prompt about a quest why the quest exists, as a small slice computed by code from stored ids (the intent it serves, what it builds, ideals, metrics and gaps) with the structure to drill into. Avoid: injecting whole specifications, any model call to build the slice, and charging a person who has no intents.
milestones: 1. Intent-grounded pass rate: recorded for each arm of the single-call ladder.
knowledge: The backend builds the frame (app/business/intents/frame.py) and serves it at the intents frame endpoint; the autopilot brief, the chat quest facts and the quest card carry it. Gaps are queries over ids, never model judgments.
measures_of_success: A larger share of cases whose right answer depends on the intent are answered correctly with the frame than without, at small extra input cost, and cases with no intent are unchanged. Standing conditions: Keep the slice under a fixed small token ceiling. Add nothing for an unsorted quest or a person with no intents.
parameters: The slice carries a fixed token ceiling and names the card of the intent so the model can drill in; the carrier is chosen per surface.
inputs: A quest id and the viewer.
outputs: Frame text, an anchor (intent, solution, implementation, quest ids) and what sits directly below it.
effects: Read-only database queries on the backend; no model call; the autopilot brief grows by the frame only when the quest is placed.
usage_notes: Selection stays on the no-frame arm until the intent-grounded metric has been run by decision; the paid ladder is staged under esoi/metric-run-policy.md.

name: Specification slice before a task and write-back after
scoped_purpose: Use for: starting a task from the slice of the specification it serves and leaving what it learned in the fields that already exist (a solution's gap and action, recorded metric rows). Avoid: new documents per session and any write the person did not make possible.
knowledge: Repositories already carry records with a gap and an action per solution; the standing deep-run instructions carry the generic method today.
measures_of_success: More tasks accepted on the first attempt and fewer reads before the first edit on the second task for the same solution, with no new files outside the records. Standing conditions: Create no new file outside the records and the code.
parameters: The slice size per solution; whether write-back is done by the worker in the same change.
inputs: A task, its quest or its working folder.
outputs: A slice for the brief and updated gap, action and metric rows.
effects: Edits to existing record fields in the same commit as the change; no model call of its own.

name: Core ML tasks: quest classification and recommendation
scoped_purpose: Use for: classifying a quest or an input (which quest it belongs to, what kind of ask it is) and recommending what comes next (a goal, a step, a quest), anywhere in Quest, with the implementation chosen by measurement. Avoid: routing a chat message to answer, tool or deep (route-a-message) and ranking theory in Concept AI (rank-theories).
milestones: 1. Accuracy of core ML tasks: accuracy recorded on held-out labelled cases for shared-quest-ranker against hybrid-candidate-ranker, then for the area-of-life and recommendation alternatives.
knowledge: Requested by Joshua on 2026-10-19: quest classification and recommendation are the main ML tasks used across Quest and have had alternative implementations. Located in code on 2026-10-19: which-quest classification in quest-backend quest_selection.py (the shared ranker) and quest_candidates.py (the chat's hybrid ranker); area-of-life classification in categories/search.py and planets_service.py; quest-to-intent placement and intent recommendation in intents/suggest.py; next-period goal placement in period_review_ai.py; message routing in evaluation/components/classification.
measures_of_success: Each task has a labelled case set with a held-out share, and every alternative has a recorded result on it; the selected alternative is the best by accuracy with cost as tie-break.
parameters: The task (classify or recommend), the implementation, and the model tier where one is used.
inputs: The quest, input text or user data to classify, or the person's quests, goals and history to recommend from.
outputs: A class or a ranked list with a score for each, and the cost of producing it.
effects: May spend model tokens; reads user data; writes nothing.
usage_notes: Define a case set per task first, then register each existing alternative as an implementation of this solution.

name: Select the intent specifications an input concerns
scoped_purpose: Use for choosing, from an ESOI specification index, the few records a new use case or input concerns, with their linked records. It avoids building the index (the ESOI library does, without AI), avoids reading records in full (the caller does, for the chosen ones), and avoids choosing context cards for files (select-context does).
knowledge: The ESOI specification index (version 1 JSON: entries, weighted terms, document frequencies); TF-IDF and reciprocal rank fusion; parallel batched LLM selection as in the card filter.
measures_of_success: On labelled inputs every expected record is selected; a failed vector or model call never removes a candidate; calls equal batches. Standing conditions: The records an input concerns are selected from the whole tree in one model call's latency, with no invented ids and no loss when a call fails.
parameters: k_lexical, k_vector, batch_size, max_workers, expand, model.
inputs: The request text, the loaded index, an optional model provider, an optional vector search callable returning entry ids.
outputs: A SpecSelection: ids best first then linked ids, the candidates shown to the model, which source proposed each, the number of calls and failed batches.
effects: One cheap model call per batch of candidates; none without a provider.
usage_notes: Load the index with load_spec_index (write it with `esoi spec index --out FILE`; its digest says when it is stale), pass the run's provider and the consumer's own vector search over the same entries, then read in full only the returned ids.
verdict_detail: within the stated margin of lexical_only, lexical_vector: pass rate inside 10 percentage points and spend inside 15% (sampled, model-judged runs move that much between re-runs), so the metric does not separate them

name: Card store growth control
scoped_purpose: Use for: keeping a card store at one card per distinct source-file group: cleaning up a store that inflated (moving duplicates out of the index, never deleting them), preventing re-import compounding at bootstrap, and telling the operator loudly when a store passes its expected size. Avoid: a hard card quota that drops real knowledge, choosing which cards suit a task (select-context), and touching a card another system manages or a person taught.
milestones: 1. Cards per source-file group 1.0, duplicate share 0 and no group lost on every card_growth case, for the cleanup tool and then for the bootstrap guards on the same cases. 2. A store built by repeated passes with the guards on passes every case with no cleanup run over it.
knowledge: The copy-import id rule (a namespace of the source root, two dashes, the card id, cut to 200 characters) with copies of copies kept is what compounded (docs/context-card-stores.md, containment audit defects 1 and 2). Two real stores reached 8,557 and 32,070 cards on 2026-10-05 and were cleaned by moving cards into _quarantine. Mount mode stops copying for the stores that adopt it. A compounded copy can be the only copy left, so it is moved only when a surviving card with the same files stays (scripts/quarantine_cards.py).
measures_of_success: Every card_growth case keeps one card per source-file group, loses no group and keeps the taught and managed cards. Standing conditions: Move cards, never delete them. Never remove a card a person taught or another system manages, except a provable compounded copy. Impose no fixed quota; give a loud notice instead.
parameters: Cleanup: the reasons to apply, the file-set overlap at which two cards count as one, excluded and kept folder prefixes, other stores that cover this one, and dry run or apply. Notice: the card count at which the operator is told (a default of 1000 is being built).
inputs: A card store directory, its folder review, and optionally other stores to compare it with.
outputs: A manifest naming every card moved, or that would move, with its reason and the card that keeps its knowledge, and a printed report.
effects: Moves card files under the store's _quarantine folder by reason; the store ignores that folder, so the index shrinks and a move is undone by moving the file back.
usage_notes: Run the cleanup as a dry run first, read the manifest, then apply it. A lane in copy mode should move to mount mode (docs/context-card-stores.md, Migrating a deployment) so the cause stops; the cleanup removes what already happened.
verdict_detail: passes more cases than no_cleanup

name: Unified card and specification search
scoped_purpose: Use for: selecting, for one run, the context cards and the ESOI records it concerns in one pipeline (one lexical stage, one vector stage, one fusion, one cheap-model choice, one budget) and handing them to the run labelled with their kind. Avoid: copying a record into a card store (a record is a read-only view of its row, as a mounted card is a view of its owner's card), editing records (track-runs-on-records proposes changes), and building either index (the card store and the ESOI library do).
milestones: 1. A combined labelled case set exists: requests whose right answer mixes cards and records, beside the existing context_selection and spec_selection cases. 2. The merged pipeline at or above the recorded spec_selection balanced score and context_selection pass rate on their own cases, and ahead of the two separate pipelines on the mixed cases.
knowledge: How the two pipelines differ today, stage by stage. Candidates: cards from the card repository; records from the ESOI spec index, rebuilt when a record file changes. Lexical: IDF over a card's name, keywords, summary, terms, symbols and content (adapters/context_store_assembly.py), against field-weighted TF-IDF over the index's own terms (core/spec_selection.py). Vector: the card vector store or the Quest backend's search, against an injected local embedder over record lines (core/repo_specs.py). Fusion: weighted reciprocal-rank fusion with keyword above vector (adapters/hybrid_context_assembler.py), against plain reciprocal-rank fusion. Choice: a balanced-tier filter and a consolidation pass (core/card_filter.py), against a confidence gate that calls a model only for an unclear case. Output: a card result carries no kind, a record result does. Wiring: cards are assembled at the start of every run (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); records only through tools (core/tools_repo_specs.py) or the deep-goal slice (core/spec_slice.py). A mounted store is read in place and never copied; the same principle holds for records.
measures_of_success: On the mixed cases the expected cards and records are in view under one budget; on each half neither existing metric drops; an assembly makes one model call or none. Standing conditions: Never copy a record into a card store. Label every result with its kind and its source.
parameters: Candidate pool size per source, fusion weights per source and kind, the gate thresholds, which record kinds are ranked directly and which are reached through links, the shared character budget, and the assembly deadline.
inputs: The task text and run metadata (scope tags, deadline), the card repository and vector store, and the ESOI spec index of the repository root when one is found.
outputs: One assembled context: ranked items, each with its kind (card, or a record kind), source and id, the rendered view under one budget, and the sources for the answer's explanation.
effects: Reads cards and records and writes neither; at most one cheap model call, none for a clear or an empty case.
usage_notes: Planned: nothing is built and nothing is selected. Today the two pipelines run side by side (two_pipelines). Which record kinds become ranked views is decided by this solution's metric between the planned arms, and the owner of the specification approves the choice.

name: Per-record run tracking and change proposals
scoped_purpose: Use for: updating, after every run, the record the run served (a context card or an ESOI record) with the run that touched it, its outcome, the metric movement and what moved, and filing a proposed change to a record when the work shows it is wrong or missing, as one tracked item for the record's owner. It is the update-back shape cards already use (usage, outcome, provenance), applied to every record. Avoid: editing a specification record without its owner's approval, a new file per run, and judging whether a change was good (the metric does).
milestones: 1. Every deep run on a solution with an offline arm leaves a durable before and after reading on that solution. 2. Every run that touched a record leaves its outcome and movement on that record. 3. Every proposed record change reaches its owner as one tracked item.
knowledge: Already true: record_metric_result and GoalMetrics give a deep run a recorded or measured before and after per metric (core/tools_metric_results.py, core/goal_metrics.py, core/metric_meter.py); the executor puts metrics and metric_missing on the task report (runner/executor_reporting.py); FileContextStore.record bumps a card's usage_count, sets last_outcome from the turn kind and stamps provenance (adapters/context_store_cards.py). Missing: the ledger is per run in a temporary folder; no field says what moved; readings never reach the record; the card updater gets no metric facts; no proposal path exists. One home per kind already exists: the results log for metric readings, the tracker files with their hand-edited tracking_status, tracking_owner, tracking_updated and tracking_notes columns for ESOI records, and a card's own usage fields for cards.
measures_of_success: Runs on measured solutions leave durable, attributed readings and say what moved; proposals reach the owner as tracked items. Standing conditions: Never edit a specification record without its owner's approval. Create no file per run.
parameters: Which records a run updates (the ones it was shown and used), whether a reading is recorded or measured, where proposals are delivered (the escalation sink), and who owns each specification.
inputs: The run's metric results (metric, solution, milestone, before, after), what it changed, the records it was shown and used, and any proposal it made.
outputs: Per record: the last run that touched it, its outcome, the metric movement, what moved, and a pending proposal if any; for the owner, the proposals awaiting a decision.
effects: Writes a card's usage fields and provenance; appends readings to the results log; updates the tracker row's tracking columns; raises a decision request for a proposal. Never edits a specification record itself.
usage_notes: Planned: today's pieces are recorded as per_run_ledger. The owner of a specification approves every change to it; an AI proposes.
